name: Radiohead
hook: A guitar band whose singer stopped listening to guitar music, played Warp records instead, and turned the band into something closer to Aphex Twin and Can for 'Kid A'.
blurb: Radiohead formed at school in Abingdon, near Oxford, in 1985 as On a Friday: Thom Yorke, Jonny and Colin Greenwood, Ed O'Brien and Philip Selway. They signed to EMI in December 1991. Their first hit, 'Creep' (1992), was a loud guitar song that was a hit around the world, and they came to resent it. 'OK Computer' (1997) was much stranger, and Yorke has said Miles Davis's 'Bitches Brew' influenced it. By the late 1990s Yorke had turned away from rock and melody and was listening almost only to electronic music from the Warp label, like Aphex Twin and Autechre, because it had structure and no singing in it. On 'Kid A' (2 October 2000), produced with Nigel Godrich, the band used drum machines, modular synthesizers, an early electronic instrument called the ondes Martenot, and editing on computers in Pro Tools and Cubase, as much as guitars. They also named Can, Charles Mingus, Alice Coltrane, Miles Davis, Talking Heads' 'Remain in Light' and Björk's 'Homogenic' as influences. In 2007 they released 'In Rainbows' online themselves and let fans pay whatever they wanted, even nothing, the first time a major act had done that.
